newsitem.title: CHINA: China says must keep pressure on Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says must keep pressure on Taiwan.

text.p: Chinese military manouevres and missile exercises near Taiwan early this year achieved results but Beijing must maintain pressure on the island, the official media reported on Saturday.
The China News Service quoted a specialist in Taiwan affairs as saying that Beijing's policies -- including its show of force in March -- had struck a blow against Taiwan independence.

"In order to resolve the Taiwan question in the future it is essential to maintain a certain degree of pressure while stepping up contacts with people from Taiwan," the news agency quoted Li Jiachuan of the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, a top think tank, as saying.
The agency said he told a conference on relations with Taiwan that Beijing's war games had demonstrated to the world that China had the willpower and the ability to protect its territorial integrity.
China and Taiwan have been at loggerheads since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949 when the Nationalist government fled to the island after its defeat on the mainland by the communists.
China views Taiwan as a rebel province and refuses to rule out the use of force to achieve its goal of reunification.
Beijing held war games near Taiwan in March in a bid to intimidate voters ahead of the island's first direct presidential elections.
The United States sent warships near the island in its own show of force to ensure the polls were not disrupted.
Other political experts at the Beijing conference said that China and Taiwan were now focusing on the need for talks on reunification.
The report did not mention that Beijing broke off the semi-official talks last year in anger over a private visit to the United States by Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui.
